hypothesis: Writing a durable dispatch intention before backend entry prevents a one-shot FDB collection from omitting running or crashed tool attempts.
limitations: A crash between intention persistence and backend entry can leave a record for an action not entered; this is not exactly-executed or exactly-once evidence.
Unfinished records omit timestamp_end and use status unconfirmed. Final end timestamps mark executor observation end, not confirmed backend effects.
Upstream scores function and args without using confirmation status; a passing tool-call score does not prove successful effects.
The atomic compatibility snapshot rewrites retained history under a cooperative cross-process lock; it costs O(history), measured separately in dispatch-io-cost.json.
Process-exit persistence is tested. Power-loss durability and noncooperating external writers are not validated.
If start persistence fails, dispatch is prevented and an explicit tool_log_error is emitted. Completion persistence failure leaves unconfirmed intention while preserving the actual backend outcome.
